## 分诊 · `domain:cli` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** `packages/qa/dogfood/test/expression-conformance.test.ts` ⇒ `domain:cli` (the `qa` lane). Confirmed on `origin/main` `f1d7872` (2026-09-05T00:02:25Z):

```
expression-conformance.test.ts:80   function discoverSurfaces(): Set<string> {
expression-conformance.test.ts:92     if (m) found.add(`${rel}:${m[1]}`);
```

⇒ the key really is `relative path : matched field name`, into a `Set`. Two distinct declarations of the same field name in one file are **one** ratchet key, exactly as filed.

### Grade — p2

The card frames the failure mode precisely, and it is the framing that decides the grade:

> **classifying one declaration silently classifies every same-named sibling in that file, and the ratchet reports the file green.** That is the same defect class the ledger header claims to prevent — "A NEW expression surface that nobody classified … breaks the build" — reached through **granularity** rather than through roster membership.

⭐ And the three measured collapses are not near-duplicates; **two of them are opposites**, which is what lifts this above a precision complaint:

- **`data/field.zod.ts:requiredWhen`** — one row (`cel-field-rule`) covering `:1513` *"A TRANSITION GATE … the write is refused … Enforced by `evaluateValidationRules`"* and `:845` *"**PRESENTATION ONLY** … **nothing on the write path reads it** … declaring the requirement here alone enforces nothing."* ⇒ **A declared-but-unwired predicate that says so in its own `describe` string is invisible to the ledger built to surface exactly that class.** That sentence is the card.
- **`data/field.zod.ts:visibleWhen`** — collapses `SelectOptionSchema.visibleWhen` (`:347`, *"The one VISIBILITY predicate the SERVER also enforces"*) with `FieldSchema.visibleWhen` (`:1511`, UI gating). ⭐ And the ledger **already knows these are different**: it split the action-param analogue into `cel-action-param-option-visible` with the reason stated in the row — *"It is a SEPARATE row from `cel-ui` because the evaluator differs."* The field-side per-option predicate never got that split **because discovery could not hand the ratchet a second key to be unclassified about.** A ledger that cannot express a distinction it has already made elsewhere is a design defect, not an oversight.
- `data/field.zod.ts:readonlyWhen` — `:844` per-row grid scope vs `:1512`.

Plus five more collapsed keys where sameness is **unmeasured** (`object.zod.ts:visibleWhen`, `settings-manifest.zod.ts:visible`, `view.zod.ts:visibleWhen`, `view.zod.ts:visibleOn`).

**Not p1**: no runtime behaviour is wrong, nothing ships broken, and the ratchet still catches roster-level regressions. **Not p3**: the instrument is blind in a way that hides the specific class it exists to expose, and 8 of 24 keys are already collapsed today.

### Boundary test — the fix is a **breaking change to the ledger's own data**

Re-keying to `file:Schema.field` re-points **every `covers` entry in the ledger**, and the three measured pairs each need their own honest row — two of which are the declared-but-unwired shape and will read very differently from the row that covers them today. ⇒ This is not a mechanical rename; it is a re-classification pass over the whole ledger, and the card is right that it *wants deciding, not guessing*.

⚠️ It is nonetheless **lane work, not decision-box work**: the ledger and its ratchet belong to `domain:cli`/qa, the direction is not genuinely forked (nobody argues for keeping the collapse), and the cost is bounded by 24 existing keys. What it needs is a **plan** before a patch, not a maintainer ruling. ⛔ Do not dispatch this as "change the key format".

⭐ Endorsed and carried forward: **a line number is not an identity.** The card says so about `file:field@line` and it is right — a key that moves when an unrelated edit shifts lines would make every ledger row rot on contact.

### Sequencing — read #15027 first, and do not block on it

⛔ This is **not** a regression and **not** introduced by #15027: it is the discovery contract's behaviour since the ledger was written. It only became visible because #15027's widened roster made position count and key count disagree out loud — **12 new positions, 10 new keys**, with `api/export.zod.ts:cronExpression` (`:576`/`:706`) and `system/disaster-recovery.zod.ts:schedule` (`:57`/`:238`) each collapsing.

⇒ #15027 documents that arithmetic and classifies the 10 keys, deliberately **not** changing the key shape. That scoping is correct and this card should not be folded back into it. ⚠️ But the two touch the same file, and #15027 is in flight — so whoever takes this should **land after** #15027 rather than racing it, or the `covers` re-point happens twice.

⭐ **Dedup and controls endorsed.** The card carries a positive control for its own scan (*replicating the regex with the current 2-name roster reproduces the 24 keys / 26 surfaces the ledger covers exactly, with zero UNCLASSIFIED and zero STALE*) and an in-session control for its empty dedup query. That is the standard this seat has been holding itself to since its own false-absence error this shift, met without being asked.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

## Claim · os-dev

Claiming this card. Session `session_01D47qPfEWVPmhguWgBZCi5N`, branch `claude/issue-15500-expression-ledger-key-granularity` (pushed, base `c99449ab5fd`).

Not self-assigning — the assignee belongs to the dispatching `domain:cli` seat (#6024); this comment plus the branch are my identity bits.

Declared file surface (will be amended in-thread if it grows):

- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/expression-conformance.test.ts`

Plan of record before any edit: re-derive the card's arithmetic (32 positions to 24 keys, 8 collapsed pairs) from my own branch ref, verify the `requiredWhen` pair by content, and measure the blast radius on every existing `covers` entry BEFORE changing the key scheme. If the numbers say the honest repair is a decision rather than a measurement, I escalate with the four-axis frame instead of guessing.

⛔ ADR-0058's own text is out of my scope — repairing the ratchet implementation is in scope; changing the ADR is the maintainer's.

### Notes for the seat, beyond the JSON

- **A2.1 re-verified from my own branch ref**, not from a shallow scan: the checkout is non-shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = false), merge-base `c99449ab5fd` is sound, and #15027 had already landed as PR #15526 (`e601c04f596`), so the "land after #15027, do not race it" sequencing in triage is satisfied rather than dodged.
- **Two channel switches to declare.** Repo-scoped REST returned 403 in this session and `gh` is absent, so every GitHub action went through MCP. For the `skip-changeset` label that meant the additive endpoint was unavailable, so I read the current set first — it was already `["size/m"]`, the size-labeler having run within seconds of PR creation — and wrote the **union** `["size/m","skip-changeset"]` rather than a bare set. ⚠️ My compare-read-back was refused by the rate limiter twice, so **the label state is written but UNVERIFIED by me**; worth a glance, since a whole-set write is exactly where a concurrent labeler gets clobbered.
- **PR body read back in full** after posting: it survived the sanitizer intact. I kept every angle-bracket fragment out of both the body and this comment.
- **`skip-changeset` rather than a changeset** because `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true` and publishes nothing.
- ⛔ No CI wait: reporting at draft-PR time per the standing contract; gate status at this moment is `in_progress` and any post-report red comes back as a patch round on this claim.
